headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risks arise from shared file-based workflows; B’s shell/write access can amplify A’s workflow outputs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A can emit workflow artifacts over REST/GRPC, and B reads/writes local files and runs shell/subprocesses. If B ingests A-produced artifacts as instructions, a file-based prompt-injection path exists. The pair lacks documented provenance or isolation, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF B parses A-generated artifacts or logs as instructions
IF A’s outputs are copied into B’s workspace without provenance checks
mitigations: Add a strict allowlist for instruction-bearing fields in B
Prefix all A outputs with non-executable metadata markers
Review one sample A artifact before B consumes it
Disable automatic ingestion of A outputs into B
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between A and B

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches artifacts and parameters, while B touches academic papers, metadata, research questions, and configuration secrets. B also has filesystem read/write plus shell execution, so shared-workspace leakage is plausible if A’s artifacts are placed where B can read them. No evidence shows isolation, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF A artifacts or parameters are stored in a workspace readable by B
IF B is configured to process files from the same directory as A
mitigations: Move A and B to separate directories
Remove secrets from any shared workspace
Check file permissions on the shared mount
Rotate any secrets present in B’s working tree
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has allowlisted network egress and API access; B has shell, subprocess, filesystem write, and allowlisted egress. They do not both have unrestricted git or filesystem write to the same dir, but overlapping mutable surfaces still create coordination risk if they share resources. Because shared-state behavior is not stated, uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF A and B target the same mutable workspace or API resource
IF B writes files that A later reads or publishes
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories
Serialize writes to any shared resource
Check for stale files before each run
Avoid concurrent runs against the same dataset
requires-engineering: add locking around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: A produces workflow outputs and B exposes agentic ask/stream endpoints, so A’s outputs could become B’s inputs in a downstream chain. There is no documented verification step or critique loop between them, but also no evidence of automatic action-taking. That supports medium rather than high.
conditions: IF B consumes A outputs as authoritative context
IF B forwards A-derived claims into downstream responses or actions
mitigations: Insert a human review step between A and B
Require B to cite source provenance for A-derived claims
Compare A outputs against a second source
Disable autonomous action-taking on A outputs
requires-engineering: add verification gates before B acts

E_compliance.rationale: B explicitly handles configuration secrets and requests Airflow credentials, while A is a workflow engine with allowlisted egress and API surfaces. The pair therefore creates a plausible compliance mismatch around secret handling and retention, even though no residency or certification mismatch is documented. Only B is cited because the issue is secret handling on B’s side.
conditions: IF secrets from B are stored in the same environment as A artifacts
IF logs or notebooks retain credentials beyond the intended session
mitigations: Remove secrets from notebooks and examples
Redact credentials from logs immediately
Store secrets in a dedicated secret manager
Review retention settings for shared logs
requires-engineering: formalize secret-handling and retention policy
